q: 101. Tractive coefficient of a Crawler truck in loose soil is ............
options: less than that of rubber tyre tractors
more than it at of rubber tyre tractors
same as that of rubber tyre tractors
explain: Crawler tracks provide a larger contact area (lower ground pressure) compared to rubber tires, allowing for better traction and a higher tractive coefficient in loose or soft soils.

q: 102. The handling of materials in the construction of a multistoreyed building will require for lifting ............
explain: A hoist is the standard equipment used in high-rise construction to vertically transport materials like bricks, mortar, and steel to different floor levels.

q: 103. The construction equipment suitable for lifting and transportation is ............
explain: Lift trucks (like forklifts) handle both lifting and short-distance transport, while spiral chutes are used for gravity-based vertical transport (transportation) of materials.

q: 104. The maximum amount of advance payment (mobilization fund) permitted is ............ of contract amount.
explain: According to standard public procurement rules, the mobilization advance is generally capped at 20% of the contract price to help the contractor start the work.

q: 105. Which part of contract documents describes the process of performing any item's of requirements?
explain: Specifications detail the quality of materials, the workmanship required, and the specific methods/processes to be followed for each item of work.

q: 106. The first stage of construction is ............
explain: Every construction project begins with the 'initiation of proposal' where the need for the project is identified and feasibility is assessed.

q: 107. Vibratory rollers are more useful for compacting which of the following ............
explain: Vibratory rollers are most effective on non-cohesive (granular) soils like sand and gravel because the vibration rearranges the particles into a denser state.

q: 108. Bottom-dump wagons are suitable for handling which of the following ............
explain: Bottom-dump wagons are ideal for free-flowing materials like sand and gravel. They are unsuitable for wet clay because it tends to stick to the sides and won't discharge easily.

q: 109. Which one of the following rollers is suitable for soil cement stabilized road construction?
explain: Pneumatic tired rollers provide a 'kneading' action which is excellent for finishing base courses and soil-cement stabilized layers.

q: 110. The most suitable type of equipment for compaction of cohesive soils is
explain: Sheep's foot rollers compact by 'kneading' and applying high pressure, which is essential for breaking down bonds in cohesive soils like clay.

q: 111. A crusher which can be used as either primary or secondary crusher is ............
explain: Hammer mills are versatile impact crushers that can be adjusted to serve as either primary or secondary reduction units depending on the feed size and desired output.

q: 112. Price adjustment in any contract will be done if price change exceeds by ............
explain: Standard contract clauses usually trigger price adjustments only when the fluctuation in the cost of materials or labor exceeds a 10% threshold.

q: 113. The best method of procurement for complex and work of specific nature is ............
explain: International Competitive Bidding (ICB) is preferred for complex projects to ensure a wide range of expert bidders and competitive global pricing.

q: 114. A concrete mixer is specified by ............
options: The volume of the mixing drum
volume of mixed concrete discharges after mixing of each batch
explain: Mixers are designated by the volume of unmixed materials (input) and the volume of mixed concrete they can discharge (output) per batch (e.g., 200/140 liters).

q: 115. The horse power of driving motor of a 5 cubic metre concrete mixer would be about ............
explain: A standard concrete mixer around this capacity typically requires a motor in the range of 5 HP for efficient operation.

q: 116. Material used for the construction of load bearing piles is ............
explain: Piles can be made of timber (wood), reinforced concrete, or steel sections depending on the load and soil conditions.

q: 117. Which of the following equipments is not used for hauling ............
explain: A dragline is an excavating machine, not a hauling machine. While it can move material within its reach, it does not transport material over distances.

q: 118. During the construction period, price variation clause in contracts caters to ............
options: increase in rates of only important materials
variation in cost in materials element, labour element and petrol-oil-lubricant element
variation in total cost of the project on an ad hoc basis
explain: A comprehensive price variation clause accounts for fluctuations in the core cost components: labor, materials, and fuel (POL).

q: 119. At a work site, statistical quality control of concrete means ............
options: measurement of risks to eliminate failures
applying the theory of probability to sample testing or inspection
reduction in wastage of inspection costs
reduction in costs for the removal of defects
explain: Statistical quality control involves testing a representative sample and using probability to determine if the entire batch meets specifications.

q: 120. Mobilization advance up to 10% of the cost of work is given to a contractor ............
options: on commencement of work at site for payment of loan taken by him
for the purchase of construction materials
for the payment of advances to labour and other staff
for all activities required to start the work at site on finalization of the contract document
explain: Mobilization advance is specifically provided to help the contractor with initial expenses like setting up site offices, moving machinery, and procuring initial supplies.

q: 121. Security deposit deducted at 5% from contractor's bills is ............
options: refunded when the contractor has completed the work
refunded even before the completion of the work provided good progress has been established
retained till the expected life of the structure of say 100 years and spent for maintenance
refunded when the defect liability period of six months or one monsoon whichever is later is over
explain: The security deposit (retention money) is held to ensure the contractor fixes any defects that appear during the Defect Liability Period (DLP).

q: 122. Sinking fund is ............
options: the fund for rebuilding a structure when its economic life is over
the total sum to be paid to the municipal authorities by the tenants
a part of the money kept in reserve for providing additional structure and structural modifications
explain: A sinking fund is a sum set aside periodically so that at the end of the utility period of the asset, sufficient funds are available for its replacement.

q: 123. Which of the following conveyor is never used?
explain: All the listed types (Spiral, Roller, and Screw) are standard conveyors used in various industrial and construction material handling applications.

q: 124. A canal is trimmed on its side and bottom by ............
explain: Mechanical trimmers are specialized machines used to precisely finish the slopes and beds of canals before lining.

q: 125. The amount saved as depreciation reserve fund will be termed as ............
explain: Depreciation is an internal accounting provision for the wear and tear of an asset; it is not classified as profit, loss, or direct operating cost in this context.

q: 126. The direct cost of a project with respect normal time is ............
explain: At normal time, the project is executed using the most efficient methods and standard resources, resulting in the lowest possible direct cost.

q: 127. The reduction in project time normally results in ............
options: decreasing the direct cost and increasing indirect cost
increasing the direct cost and decreasing the indirect cost
increasing the direct cost and indirect cost both
decreasing the direct cost and indirect cost both
explain: Crashing (reducing time) increases direct costs due to overtime and extra resources, but decreases indirect costs like overheads and supervision because the project duration is shorter.

q: 128. Economic saving of time result by crashing ............
explain: To reduce project duration economically, we always crash the activity on the critical path that has the lowest cost slope (the cheapest to compress).

q: 129. The process of incorporating changes and rescheduling or preplanning is called ............
explain: Updating is the process of re-evaluating the project network periodically to account for actual progress and making necessary adjustments to future schedules.

q: 130. Slack time refers to ............
explain: In PERT/CPM, 'Slack' is a term specifically used for events (nodes), while 'Float' is the term used for activities.

q: 131. Which of the following is the correct from of representation of an event?
explain: In a network diagram, an event (a point in time marking the start or end of an activity) is standardly represented by a circle or a node.

q: 132. Which of the following is not related to cost slope?
explain: Cost slope is calculated using (Crash Cost - Normal Cost) / (Normal Time - Crash Time). Slack is a time-related buffer for events and is not part of the cost slope formula.

q: 133. Use of dummies is required for ............
explain: Dummy activities consume zero time and resources; they are used solely to maintain the correct logic and dependencies between activities in a network.

q: 134. In a line organization ............
options: responsibility of each individual is fixed
explain: Line organization is the simplest form where authority flows vertically, ensuring clear accountability, strict discipline, and rapid decision-making.

q: 135. Number of pre-operation associated with an operation may be ............
explain: An activity or operation can have multiple predecessor (pre-operation) activities that must be completed before it can begin.

q: 136. The post-operations in C.P.M. are marked ............
explain: In a left-to-right network flow, succeeding activities (post-operations) are positioned to the right of the current activity arrow.

q: 137. In C.P.M. method, the earliest finish is indicated by time on ............
options: top right, outside the circle, in triangle
top right, outside the circle, in rectangle
explain: Standard CPM notation often uses a rectangle for Earliest Start/Finish times and a triangle for Latest Start/Finish times located near the event nodes.

q: 138. Latest finish time in C.P.M. technique is indicated by a ............
explain: According to the provided answer key (and common CPM chart standards), the rectangle is used to represent the boundary times like Latest Finish.

q: 139. The quality assurance plan is prepared and submitted by ............
explain: The contractor is responsible for ensuring the quality of the work and must submit a Quality Assurance Plan (QAP) to the client/consultant for approval.

q: 140. The essential condition for the decompression of an activity is that ............
options: the project time should change due to decompression
after decompression, the time of an activity invariably exceeds its normal time
an activity could be decompressed to the maximum extent of its normal time
explain: Decompression is the reverse of crashing. You can only expand an activity's duration back to its original 'Normal Time' but not beyond it.

q: 141. Dummy activities are used to ............
explain: Dummies are structural tools in a network diagram used to show relationships (logic) when two activities share the same start and end nodes.

q: 142. Which of the following are the guidelines for the construction of a network diagram?
options: each activity is represented by one only arrow in the network
dangling must be avoided in a network diagram
dummy activity consumes no time or resource
explain: These are fundamental rules: unique arrows per activity, avoiding loose ends (dangling), and utilizing zero-duration dummies for logic.

q: 143. Due to omission of any part of a project, the duration of project will ............
explain: Removing a scope of work (omission) generally reduces the total amount of work to be done, thereby decreasing the project duration.

q: 144. Due to omission of any part of a project, the cost of project will ............
explain: If a portion of the project is removed, the direct costs associated with those materials and labor are subtracted from the total project cost.

q: 145. Who is responsible for accident occurred at worksite?
explain: The main contractor is legally and contractually responsible for safety management and any accidents that occur within the site premises during construction.

q: 146. The main criteria for selection of contractors to execute work is ............
explain: Pre-qualification and selection involve evaluating a contractor's financial stability, technical expertise, available equipment, and past project experience.

q: 147. Best option to avoid the undue pressure, cartels and collusion during bidding process is ............
explain: Electronic bidding (E-bidding) increases transparency and prevents physical cartels or collusion between bidders because the process is digitized and hidden until the deadline.

q: 148. Which is not the part of bidding documents ............
explain: While the Invitation for Bid (IFB) advertises the project, the 'Bidding Documents' usually refer to the technical and legal package (drawings, specs, contract) provided to the bidder.

q: 149. Batching refers to ............
options: controlling the total quantity at each bath
weighing accurately, the quantity of each material for a job before mixing
controlling the quantity of each material into each batch
adjusting the water to be added in each batch according to the moisture content
explain: Concrete batching is the process of measuring and controlling the proportions of cement, aggregates, and water for every single mix cycle (batch).

q: 150. Cost of owning an equipment would include ............
options: cost of depreciation, maintenance and repair and fuel
cost of investment, wages of the crew and fuel
cost of fuel, lubricating oil, investment and depreciation
cost of investment, major repairs and depreciation
explain: Owning costs (fixed costs) include the initial investment, interest, taxes, insurance, depreciation, and major storage/overhaul, whereas fuel and wages are operating costs.

q: 151. Sensitivity analysis is a study of .............
options: change in output due to change in input
economics of cost and benefits of the project
explain: Sensitivity analysis determines how different values of an independent variable (input) affect a particular dependent variable (output) under a given set of assumptions.

q: 152. With the usual notations, sinking fund factor is given by .............
explain: The sinking fund factor is the amount of money to be set aside annually to accumulate a certain sum of money at the end of a given period at a given interest rate.

q: 153. In the time-cost optimisation, using C.P.M. method for network analysis, the crashing of the activities along the critical path is done starting with the activity having .............
explain: To minimize the increase in project cost while shortening the duration, activities on the critical path with the lowest cost slope (least expensive to crash) are prioritized.

q: 154. Preliminary project report for a road project must contain .............
options: the detailed estimated cost based on detailed design
the several alternatives of the project that have been considered
the soil survey, traffic survey, concept design and approximate cost
the contract documents for inviting tenders
explain: A preliminary report focuses on feasibility and basic data like soil types, traffic volume, and rough cost estimates before moving to detailed design.

options: a large dam constructed across a river for a single or multi-purpose
any job involving many people and large money
a work of major importance involving huge men and material
an organised team work to achieve a set task within the time limit
explain: A project is defined by its temporary nature (time limit) and its specific goal-oriented organization.

q: 156. Technology is the .............
options: study of machines and their operation
study of behaviour men and machines
explain: In a construction context, technology refers to the practical application of knowledge regarding machines, tools, and operational methods.

q: 157. An activity is .............
options: an element of work entailed in the project
the movement of heavy vehicles from one place to another
the beginning or the end of a specified job
the progress of work up to certain limit
explain: In network analysis, an activity is a specific task or element of work that consumes time and resources.

options: the start and/or finish of an activity or the group of activities
explain: An event represents a point in time indicating the start or completion of one or more activities; it does not consume time or resources.

q: 159. The pictorial representation of activities and events of a project is known as the .............
explain: A project network is a graphical flow diagram showing the sequence of activities and their interdependencies.

q: 160. The flow of time in a net work is generally .............
explain: Standard network conventions dictate that the project timeline progresses from left (start) to right (finish).

q: 161. Bar chart is also known as .............
explain: Bar charts used in project management were developed by Henry Gantt and are widely referred to as Gantt charts.

q: 162. Bar chart is drawn for .............
explain: A Bar/Gantt chart plots individual activities on the vertical axis against a time scale on the horizontal axis.

options: a rule or a set of rules never to be violated
a definite route along which one has to proceed
a procedure for preparing the project report
a set of board guidelines stipulated by management
explain: Policies are high-level principles or guidelines that guide decision-making and organizational behavior.

q: 164. During excavation of earth work, supports are necessarily required if the depth of excavation is more than .............
explain: Standard safety regulations usually require shoring or timbering for excavations exceeding 4 feet (or approx 1.2 meters) to prevent cave-ins.

q: 165. Systematic reporting of work progress is the main objective of .............
explain: A flow process chart is used to track the sequence of all operations, transportations, inspections, and delays in a process to report and analyze progress.

q: 166. A written offer submitted by contractors to execute certain work at certain rates within the fixed time is called .............
explain: A tender (or bid) is the formal offer submitted by a contractor in response to an invitation to carry out work at a specified price.

q: 167. Which of the following is a primary process for procurement of goods and services from a competitive market?
explain: Bidding is the standard competitive process used by organizations to select vendors or contractors based on price and capability.

q: 168. Public procurement monitoring office (P.P.M.O.) can blacklist the bidders disobeying the code of conduct upto ............. years.
explain: According to typical public procurement regulations (like those in Nepal), blacklisting can range from 1 to 3 years depending on the severity.

q: 169. The contractor shall submit an application to the employer for extension of time, stating the causes for delay, days before the expiry of contract completion date .............
explain: Standard contract conditions often specify 21 days as the window to apply for an extension before the deadline lapses.

q: 170. The employer shall pay the interim bill within ............. days after the bill submitted by the contractor.
explain: 30 days is the standard industry timeframe for processing and paying interim progress certificates.

q: 171. Maximum amount that can be paid to the contractor as a prize for the early finishing of the works is equal to .............% of the contract amount.
explain: In many procurement systems, bonus payments for early completion are capped at 10% of the total contract value.

q: 172. Percentage of retention money is equal to .............% of each payment made to the contractor.
explain: Retention money is usually deducted at 5% from each interim bill to act as a safeguard against defects.

q: 173. Which of the following is not a bid document?
explain: A Letter of Acceptance is issued *after* the bidding process is finished to signify the award of the contract; it is not part of the initial bid package.

q: 174. The purpose of bid evaluation is to evaluate .............
explain: Evaluation aims to find the bidder who meets all technical requirements (substantially responsive) at the best price.

q: 175. As per public the public procurement regulation 2064, who approves the prequalification criteria?
explain: In the Nepalese PPR 2064 framework, the Head of the Department (Department Chief) holds the authority to approve these criteria.

q: 176. Duty of obligation to satisfactorily perform a task that one must fulfill and which has a consequent penalty for failure is .............
explain: Responsibility is the obligation to complete assigned duties; it implies accountability for the results.

q: 177. In a sealed quotation, the successful bidder should deliver the performance security within ............. days of receipt of letter of acceptance.
explain: For sealed quotations (usually smaller works), a shorter period like 7 days is standard for providing security.

q: 178. P.E.R.T. technique of network analysis is mainly useful for .............
explain: PERT is a probabilistic technique designed for projects with high uncertainty, such as R&D, where activity times aren't precisely known.

q: 179. Select the correct statement .............
options: activity arrows in a C.P.M. network are drawn to scale
the tail of an arrow represents the finish of an activity
arrow head represents the start of an activity
explain: None are correct: Arrows aren't drawn to scale, the tail is the start, and the head is the finish.

q: 180. Which of the following is a weakness of bar chart?
explain: Bar charts struggle to show complex relationships (interdependencies), don't handle uncertainty well, and can be difficult to update for progress.

q: 181. Which of the following is not a P.E.R.T. event?
explain: 'Class is being attended' is an ongoing process (activity), not a specific point in time (event).

q: 182. In P.E.R.T. analysis, the time estimates of activities and probability of their occurrence follow .............
explain: PERT assumes activity durations follow a Beta distribution to account for skewness in optimistic/pessimistic times.

q: 183. For excavating utility trenches with precise control of depth, the excavation equipment used is .............
explain: A backhoe (or hoe) is the most effective for trenching because it works below its own track level with high precision.

q: 184. The basic action involved in sheep foot rolling is .............
explain: Sheep foot rollers provide a kneading action, which is essential for compacting cohesive (clayey) soils.

q: 185. The remuneration of dispute adjudication board is paid by .............
explain: To ensure impartiality, the costs of a DAB are typically shared equally (50/50) between the Employer (Client) and the Contractor.

q: 186. The money deposited by the contractor as the guarantee of tender is known as .............
explain: Bid bond and earnest money are both terms for the security deposit required when submitting a tender.

q: 187. Free float is mainly used to .............
options: identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total float of succeeding activity
identify the activities, which can be delayed without affecting the start of succeeding activity
identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total of either the preceding of succeeding activities
explain: Free float is the amount of time an activity can be delayed without delaying the Earliest Start (ES) of any immediate successor.
CPM is a deterministic model using a single, certain time estimate for each activity.
PERT uses three time estimates (Optimistic, Most Likely, Pessimistic) to calculate expected time.

q: 190. Which of the following is done first in procurement of consulting services .............
explain: Expression of Interest (EOI) is the first step to identify capable firms before shortlisting and requesting a formal proposal (RFP).

q: 191. A milestone chart .............
options: shows the inter dependence of various jobs
shows the events in chronological, but in a logical sequence
explain: Milestone charts focus on key project events (milestones) chronologically, though they don't show interdependencies as well as networks.

q: 192. Time estimated time required to complete an activity is termed as .............
explain: Duration is the standard term for the time spent on performing an activity.

q: 193. The variance of the P.E.R.T. critical path is equal to .............
options: sum of variance of activities lying on critical path
maximum of sum of variance upto end event
minimum of sum of variances upto end event
explain: According to the central limit theorem, the variance of the whole path is the sum of the variances of the individual activities on that path.

q: 194. In case of burst event the latest permissible occurrence time is .............
options: maximum of LSTs of the bursting activities
maximum of ESTs of the bursting activities
minimum of LSTs of the bursting activities
minimum of ESTs of the bursting activities
explain: When moving backward through a network (backward pass), the TL (Latest Time) of a burst node is the minimum of the Latest Start Times of all outgoing activities.

q: 195. There are three parallel paths in part of a network between a bursting node and the next merging node with only one activity in each path. The minimum number of dummy arrows needed will be .............
explain: To keep the identity of activities unique (since they share the same start and end nodes), 2 dummies are required for 3 parallel activities.

q: 196. The maximum amount of project cost after the price adjustment should not exceed .............
explain: Many local regulations cap the total price adjustment (escalation) at 15% of the original contract price.

q: 197. E.O.I. is compulsory for procurement of consulting services if work amount exceeds .............
explain: As per PPR 2064, public notification for EOI is mandatory for consulting services above 2 million (20 Lakhs).

q: 198. Whenever an activity has zero total float, then .............
options: free float must be zero but independent float need not be zero
independent float must be zero but free float need not be zero
free float and independent float both must be zero
free float and independent float both need not be zero
explain: Since Independent Float ≤ Free Float ≤ Total Float, if Total Float is zero, the others must also be zero (assuming non-negative values).

q: 199. Total float for any activity is defined as the difference between .............
options: its latest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
its latest starts time and earliest start time
its latest start time and earliest finish time
its earliest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
explain: Total Float = Latest Start Time - Earliest Start Time (or LFT - EFT).

q: 200. Which one of the following is associated with a critical activity in a A-O-A network?
explain: By definition, a critical activity is one that has zero float, meaning any delay in it will delay the entire project.
